title: Loops that can shrink and loops that cannot
lede: A loop is drawn on a sphere or a torus. Slide it and watch its length. The readout says whether it can be pulled to a point without leaving the surface.
notice: On the sphere, a circle of latitude slides to the pole and its length goes to zero. Every loop on a sphere can be shrunk this way.
On the torus, the loop around the tube keeps a fixed length as it slides, and the loop around the hole never gets shorter than the inner circle. Neither can reach a point.
A small loop on the torus can still shrink. What cannot is a loop that goes around the tube or around the hole.
hint: Drag to rotate. Pick a surface and a loop, then use the slider.
